Plot STniche results

Source: R/plot_stniche.R
plot_stniche.Rd

Fifteen plot types: clusters, Zi, ranking, composition, noise, violin, zi_heatmap, celltype_heatmap, celltype_composition, celltype_stackedbar, cluster_annotation, cluster_matching, celltype_spatial, niche_signature, multi_sample_alluvial.

Usage

plot_stniche(
  x = NULL,
  samples = NULL,
  type = c("clusters", "Zi", "ranking", "composition", "noise", "violin", "zi_heatmap",
    "celltype_heatmap", "celltype_composition", "cluster_annotation", "cluster_matching",
    "celltype_spatial", "celltype_stackedbar", "niche_signature",
    "multi_sample_alluvial"),
  zi = NULL,
  gene_set = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  ptsize = 0.9,
  stroke = 0,
  reverse_y = FALSE,
  overlay_samples = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  legend_name = NULL,
  pearson_thresh = 0.6,
  jaccard_thresh = 0.15,
  top_n_spots = 200L,
  pie_top_k = 3L,
  out_dir = NULL,
  highlight_types = NULL,
  highlight_cols = NULL,
  pool_samples = FALSE,
  bar_scale = c("percent", "count"),
  top_n_celltypes = NULL,
  min_cells = 1L,
  label_min_pct = 5
)

Arguments

x

An STlist object.

samples

Character vector of sample names (or indices) to plot. Default = all samples. For type = "multi_sample_alluvial" a named list of sample groups is also accepted.

type

Character. One of the supported plot types (see details).

zi

Matrix of Local Moran Z values (rows = gene sets, columns = "sample&&libname"). Required for several plot types.

gene_set

Character. Gene set / pathway name required for type in c("Zi", "ranking", "violin").

palette

Colour palette. Can be a named character vector, a function that returns colours, or a length-3 vector/named vector for Zi gradients.

ptsize

Numeric. Point size for spatial plots.

stroke

Numeric. Point stroke width (0 = no stroke).

reverse_y

Logical. Reverse the y-axis.

overlay_samples

Logical. Overlay multiple samples in one plot when possible.

title

Character. Plot title (overrides the default title).

legend_name

Character. Legend title.

pearson_thresh

Numeric. Pearson correlation threshold (currently unused; reserved for future matching logic).

jaccard_thresh

Numeric. Jaccard index threshold (currently unused; reserved for future matching logic).

top_n_spots

Integer. Number of top spots (currently unused; reserved for future ranking logic).

pie_top_k

Integer. Number of top gene sets shown in pie charts.

out_dir

Character. Output directory (currently unused; reserved for optional file export).

highlight_types

Cell types to highlight (only for type = "celltype_spatial"). Either an unnamed character vector, or a named vector whose names are display labels and whose values are regular expressions, e.g. c(CD8 = "CD8", M2 = "M2|CD163"). Patterns are matched with grepl(..., ignore.case = TRUE) against cell_type.

highlight_cols

Named character of colours per highlighted type (names must equal the display labels).

pool_samples

Logical; for type = "celltype_stackedbar", pool all selected samples into one set of bars (default FALSE: one panel per sample).

bar_scale

"percent" (default; each bar sums to 100) or "count" (absolute number of cells per niche) for type = "celltype_stackedbar".

top_n_celltypes

Optional integer; keep the top_n_celltypes most abundant cell types and collapse the rest into "Other" (type = "celltype_stackedbar").

min_cells

Minimum number of cells a niche needs to be drawn (type = "celltype_stackedbar").

label_min_pct

Segments at least this large (in percent) are labelled with their value (type = "celltype_stackedbar").

Value

A ggplot object, a named list of them (one per sample), a ComplexHeatmap object/list, or a data frame, depending on type. "celltype_stackedbar" and "niche_signature" return a single ggplot.

Details

Why a stacked bar of cell types per niche? A niche is only biologically interpretable if its cellular make-up is known. The celltype_heatmap shows the same information as a grid, which is efficient for many cell types but makes it hard to judge how much of a niche is occupied by each type. type = "celltype_stackedbar" draws one bar per niche whose segments sum to 100\ (i) the dominant cell type(s) of every niche, and therefore its purity, can be read directly; (ii) niches can be compared side by side within a sample; and (iii) the same niche can be compared across samples (e.g. IO-naive vs IO-exposed) when several samples are supplied, which exposes sample-specific composition shifts that pooled summaries hide. Because the bars are compositional, a high share of one type is not evidence of enrichment relative to the tissue background; interpret them together with celltype_heatmap and with the niche's absolute size (printed as n under each bar).
